```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

A central TRSC design rule is that **predictive relationships are primary and
raw donor coordinates are secondary**. Redundant donors can make raw weights
nonunique even when the predictive relationship is unchanged.

```{r setup-geometry}
library(TRSC)

states <- cbind(
  A = c(-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3),
  B = c(3, 1, -1, 2, 4, 0),
  A_copy = c(-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3)
)
geometry <- trsc_geometry(states)

left <- c(A = 0.8, B = 0.2, A_copy = 0)
right <- c(A = 0, B = 0.2, A_copy = 0.8)

trsc_profile_distance(geometry, left, right)
```

Both vectors are valid simplex representations. They allocate mass differently
between duplicated donors, yet represent the same prediction function at the
supplied geometry.

## Consequence for fitted models

When `trsc_fit()` encounters a nonunique raw-coordinate solution, the optimizer
may return one numerical lift. The `weights()` method deliberately labels that
matrix as solver-selected coordinates. It should not be interpreted as a
structurally identified donor-share path unless additional identification
arguments establish that interpretation.

The package therefore avoids adding an identity ridge merely to manufacture
unique raw weights: such a coordinate penalty would alter the
representation-invariant objective.
